newsitem.title: USA: Alaska river accident kills Russian climber.
newsitem.headline: Alaska river accident kills Russian climber.

text.p: A Russian climber died while trying to cross a rushing river just a few miles shy of the end of a month-long expedition on Mount McKinley, the National Park Service said on Thursday.
Fedor Lounev, 39, of Moscow, was swept away while trying to cross a section of the rain-swollen McKinley River about midday on Wednesday, the Park Service said.
He had ascended McKinley, North America's tallest peak, from a little-used northern route that took him up the Muldrow Glacier, Park Service spokesman John Quinley said.

Lounev, with a companion, was three miles (five km) from Wonder Lake when the accident occurred, Quinley said. They had successfully crossed two sections of the braided river before the accident occurred, Quinley said.

Park rangers say crossing the roaring McKinley River is one of the most difficult parts of the Muldrow route up the mountain, Quinley said. A handful of backpackers fall into the icy river each year while hiking, but are not hindered by the heavy packs carried by mountain climbers, Quinley said.
Lounev was burdened by about 70 pounds (30 kg) of climbing gear on his back, Quinley said.
According to park ranger reports, Lounev's companion saw him carried downstream, attempted resuscitation and then hiked out to the Denali Park road and flagged down a shuttle-bus.

Rangers and park medics reached the accident scene by helicopter, Denali officials said. After trying to revive him and consulting by radio with doctors in Fairbanks, medics declared Lounev dead, park officials said.

Lounev and his companion were part of a larger Russian expedition that had hiked in by the Muldrow Glacier route about a month ago, Quinley said. The other two members were due out in two or three days, he said.
Lounev's death was the third climber fatality this year in Denali National Park.
